note: The IFC and Arab Monetary Fund's Arab Credit Reporting Guide (2015) on the Central Bank of Yemen's credit registry: banks submit data daily, written as one day; arrears are shared while they stand, and no history is stored, records being deleted once the account is updated or closed, so a late payment's mark lifts the day it's paid (clears 0) and stays while it isn't, written as thirty years, the longest the game keeps; registered as secondary, the bank's own circulars not read.

sources.title: IFC and Arab Monetary Fund, Arab Credit Reporting Guide (2015)
sources.said: institutions are required to submit data daily. ... only information on ... the current payments (on time) with balances and the arrears ... are shared and distributed. ... historical data is not stored in the CR database. ... Records are deleted once the loan account has been updated ... or if the account is closed.
